fields.name: briani
fields.description:
Rice and meat layered in the same pot with potatoes, yoghurt, mint and
saffron, then sealed with dough so nothing escapes while it cooks. Every
family swears theirs is the right one.

The potatoes at the bottom are the best part. Fight for them!
fields.long_description:
Taste: medium spice
Dietary: contains meat, usually halal

fields.name: Traditional 7 Carry
fields.description:
Seven curries served together on a banana leaf — pumpkin, beans, lentils,
chutney, pickle, rice and a sweet to finish. It comes from Tamil kitchens
and shows up at Cavadee and family prayers.

Eat it with your hands, sitting on the floor. That is how it tastes right.
fields.long_description:
Taste: mild to medium spice
Dietary: vegetarian

fields.name: Mine bouille
fields.description:
Noodles in a clear broth with vegetables and a little garlic oil, the soft
cousin of mine frite. Student food, rainy-day food, after-a-long-day food.

Ask for extra chilli paste on the side and stir it in slowly.
fields.long_description:
Taste: mild, chilli on the side
Dietary: vegetarian version usually available

fields.name: Mauritian Tea
fields.description:
Tea grown on the hills at Bois Chéri, dried with vanilla, drunk sweet and
very hot. The plantation looks over the lake and the whole south.

Take it on the terrace, no phone, and watch the mist come across the tea.

fields.name: Local Market Food Experiences
fields.description:
Flacq market runs on Wednesdays and Sundays only — the biggest on the
island. Taste your way through it with a local guide: dholl puri, fresh
fruit, pickles and hot tea, then pick up a souvenir to take home from the
craft stalls. Your guide does the bargaining.

Guide and tastings included.

fields.name: Bol Renversé
fields.description:
The magic bowl: rice/noodles packed into a bowl with chicken, vegetables and
oyster sauce, a fried egg laid on top, then flipped onto the plate at the
table. Sino-Mauritian cooking at its best.

The moment it gets turned over is half the reason you ordered it!
fields.long_description:
Taste: mild, savoury
Dietary: contains meat and egg

fields.name: Gato Piment
fields.description:
Little split-pea cakes with chilli and coriander, fried crisp and sold hot
from a paper cone. Rs 7 each, impossible to eat only one.

Best between two slices of bread with butter, standing by the stall.

fields.name: Boulette
fields.description:
Steamed dumplings — fish, chicken, chouchou, lamb — floating in a clear
broth, served with chilli and soy. Sino-Mauritian street food that has
become everybody's food.

Order a mix, drink the broth first, then take your time!
fields.long_description:
Taste: mild, chilli to taste
Dietary: contains meat or fish

fields.name: Napolitaine
fields.description:
Two rounds of shortbread with jam between them, covered in pink icing.
Buttery, sweet, and gone in three bites.

Buy four. You will not be sharing as many as you planned.

fields.name: Octopus Curry
fields.description:
Octopus cooked slowly in tomato, thyme and curry leaves until it gives up
and goes tender. Cooked on the coast and in Rodrigues, always with rice
and a good chutney.

Eat it facing the water in Mahébourg. There is no better way.

fields.name: Famous Poutou
fields.description:
Steamed rice cake with grated coconut and a little sugar, soft and warm,
wrapped in a banana leaf. Sold in the morning outside the market.

Breakfast on the way to somewhere else, eaten standing up!
fields.long_description:
Taste: lightly sweet, coconut
Dietary: vegetarian

fields.name: Fried Noodles
fields.description:
Mine frite: noodles fried hard in a wok with egg, spring onion and
whatever else is going in. Smoky, fast, and better the louder the kitchen.

Late at night, after the beach, this is the only correct order!
fields.long_description:
Taste: mild, chilli sauce on the side
Dietary: contains meat or seafood, vegetarian on request

fields.name: Caudan Food Festival
fields.description:
An evening on Caudan harbour — festival menus in the waterfront
restaurants, live music along the quay, boats and city lights behind you.
Somewhere you sit down and stay.

Organised by Caudan, so the dates change each year — check the Island
Calendar before you go. The price shown is the entry fee.

fields.name: China Town
fields.description:
Walk through Port-Louis Chinatown with a local guide and eat your way
along Royal Street: steaming dim sum, crispy gato zinzli, boulettes
served from the pot, and alouda to finish. Your guide explains how the
Sino-Mauritian community shaped the island's food, and takes you to the
small family shops visitors usually walk straight past.

Price includes the guide and all tastings. About 2 hours, small groups,
best in the morning when the shops are busiest.

fields.name: Fried Rice
fields.description:
Riz frit done the Mauritian way — rice fried with egg, chicken, prawns and
spring onion, plenty of chilli sauce on the side.

Order it to share, then quietly do not share it!
fields.long_description:
Taste: mild, savoury
Dietary: contains meat and seafood

fields.name: Alouda Pillay /food stall
fields.description:
The alouda everyone in Port-Louis argues about. Milk, basil seeds,
agar-agar jelly and a scoop of ice cream, mixed in front of you at the
Pillay stall by the market. Cold, sweet, and the best thing you can
drink after walking around the bazaar in the heat.

No rush here. Grab one, lean against the wall in the shade, watch the
market move, and let the heat pass. Then get a second one!!
fields.long_description:
Taste: sweet and cold
Dietary: vegetarian

fields.name: Halim
fields.description:
A thick soup of lentils, wheat and slow-cooked meat, topped with fried
onion, coriander and a squeeze of lemon. It comes out in Ramadan and the
queues start before sunset.

One bowl, a spoon, and absolutely nothing else to do afterwards.
fields.long_description:
Taste: medium spice
Dietary: contains meat, halal

fields.name: Gato Patate
fields.description:
Sweet potato pastry folded around sweet grated coconut and fried. Crisp
outside, soft inside, sold warm by the piece.

Rs 15 and tea. The whole afternoon sorted.

fields.name: pizzaa
fields.description:
Pizza, Port-Louis style — thin, generous, and usually eaten somewhere
nobody would call a restaurant. Chilli flakes and a bottle of Phoenix
alongside, because that is how it is done here.

Not traditional, not pretending to be. Just what everyone actually orders
on a Friday night.
fields.long_description:
Taste: mild
Dietary: contains meat, vegetarian options
